title: Airflow: make workflow dependencies visible
lead: Orchestration supports task order, failure handling, and execution evidence.
bullets: Architecture role: order dependent pipeline work.
Evidence: task state, timing, and run context.
Action: operators and source owners inspect failed dependencies.
Limit: orchestration does not supply predictive or release approval evidence by itself.
example: The required CRM validation must sit upstream of scoring and export so its failure blocks dependent work.
takeaway: Connect each tool to a responsibility, evidence, and a response owner.

title: MLflow: connect experiments and artifacts
lead: Model tracking supports reproducibility and review when evidence links are designed explicitly.
bullets: Architecture role: connect training evidence and model artifacts.
Evidence: runs, configuration, metrics, and artifact identity.
Action: reviewers compare candidates and verify compatible releases.
Limit: no single tracking tool provides every governance control.
example: Link the approved M1 to its evidence while recording B017-R1’s separate input and execution context.
takeaway: Tool records support the release decision; they do not replace its policy.

title: Validation and drift reports support diagnosis
lead: A report is useful when its reference, feature meaning, cohort, and response are clear.
bullets: Validation: test declared expectations before use.
Drift comparison: inspect change against a named reference.
Tool choice: reports can support these roles; keep policy outside the screenshot.
Action: preserve evidence and assign a response owner.
example: A missing CRM feature needs a contract-failure response; a changed valid population needs a different investigation.
takeaway: Tools make evidence easier to collect; architecture defines what that evidence means.

title: ML architecture connects five responsibilities
lead: Return to the full system and the choices that make a prediction usable.
bullets: Data: preserve meaning, validity, and temporal consistency.
Models: evaluate uncertainty and manage compatible approved artifacts.
Operations: observe, diagnose, release, and recover.
Decisions: protect access and govern appropriate business action.
example: Ana’s score becomes usable through validated inputs, traceable execution, an approved release, and a separate campaign policy.
takeaway: Day 2: foundation models and agents retain these control needs, while components and failure modes change.

title: Sources and adaptation boundaries
lead: The bibliography supplies concepts; the bank diagrams and incidents are explicit teaching applications.
bullets: Core readings: architectural decisions, serving, maintenance, and quality concerns.
Supporting readings extend monitoring, governance, and security.
Illustrations: Ana, scores, dates, batches, and incidents are invented.
Source limit: the separately catalogued checklist corrigendum remains unread.
example: No new churn outcome, repaired score, retention benefit, or real bank tool execution is claimed.
takeaway: The separate guide records reading anchors and adaptation limits.
